newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU urged to boost role in radio frequencies decisions.
newsitem.headline: EU urged to boost role in radio frequencies decisions.

text.p: The European Union and its industry should step up their presence in the global meetings that decide how to manage radio frequencies, the European Commission said on Wednesday.

The Commission said in a report that the EU needed to ensure that decisions made at World Radiocommunications Conferences (WRC) in areas such as mobile and satellite communications were in line with its own policy objectives.
The next WRC, held under the auspices of the International Telecommunications Union (ITU), is scheduled for October 27 to November 21 in Geneva.

The proposal arises in part from Commission concern over a decision on frequency allocation at the 1995 WRC that benefited Teledesic, a U.S. satellite communications venture involving Bill Gates, chairman of software giant Microsoft Corp.

The Commission report said the EU did not have a mechanism to react in a coordinated way to proposals that were introduced during WRCs -- as with the Teledesic case -- rather than prepared ahead ot time.
EU Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann has expressed concern about Teledesic becoming a "de facto monopoly".
Commission officials told reporters that EU companies were also no match for their U.S. counterparts, which actively lobby during WRCs.
"We stress the need for the industry to be more involved, particularly to give feedback if there is a change in the agenda at the conference itself," one official said.

The Commission said the EU should be more closely involved in preparing WRCs, coordinate with industry, raise political awareness and maintain contacts with third countries. The EU may need to coordinate common positions in cases where the views of its member countries initially diverge, it added.

"The importance of radiocommunications in the (EU) can be recognised when considering the penetration for cellular radiocommunications which today reaches already 30 percent in certain member states and which is expected to rise to an average of 40-50 percent throughout the (EU) by 2005," it said in a statement.
Among the items on the WRC-97 agenda are mobile and fixed satellite services, simplification of ITU radio regulations and rules applicable to broadcasting services.
